consequences: The driver thread exits, _fail_all cancels every in-flight child, and the service closes.

Every later request fails with 'hipEngine preparation failed to prepare resident session/KV cache: engine service is closed. Try a lower --max-context-tokens or --kv-storage int8_per...', which blames memory settings for a state bug.

Requests that survive a concurrent prefill report fallback_reason 'no_provider' with mtp_used false: the prompt activation never primed provider state, so the planner selects autoregressive decoding for the whole output.

blocker.exception: RuntimeError: GGUF MTP2 prompt activation claims are already reserved
blocker.summary: At concurrency >= 4 the engine service dies and every later request fails with HTTP 500. The crash is a single-slot prompt-activation guard in the MTP adapter: an incremental (multi-chunk) prefill opens prompt activation claims that stay open across ticks until the final chunk, so any other request's prompt activation raises.

reading: 19 of 24 requests never entered speculation (mtp=0, first_fallback_position=0, reason no_provider or prompt_activation_in_flight) and the rate-cliff detector found nothing to measure, because no request left speculation mid-stream.

5 requests did run MTP: three (prompts 264, 423, 645 tokens) covered 127 of 128 tokens at depth 3, and two (prompts 805, 841 tokens) emitted 123-125 autoregressive tokens first and then caught up to 2-3 speculative cycles at the end of the request. Those two report first_fallback_position=null, which is correct: the field locates the first non-speculative token after speculative output, and their speculative output came last.
So the null reading means 'no fallback after speculation' in both directions: MTP covered the tail, either from the prompt root or after a late catch-up.

concurrency_fix.remaining_gap: MTP still does not run for most concurrent requests, for reasons that are recorded rather than fatal: the serving evidence row for this cell matches only realized_group_rows == 1, so a request admitted while it is alone is later batched into a wider decode group and realizes effective_route=default; and a group mixing rows with and without a draft provider fails closed before provider mutation. 5 of 24 c=4 requests did run MTP, so the path is reachable under concurrency but not reliable.
concurrency_fix.summary: A prompt longer than max_prefill_chunk_tokens (256) holds the MTP prompt activation claim across ticks, so a second request starting its prefill hit a raise inside the driver thread, which closed the engine service. The guard now refuses only the rows that are not already streaming, records prompt_activation_in_flight on them, and keeps the engine alive.

harness_c1_reading_notes: Every request ran MTP (24 of 24) and 3,043 of 3,072 emitted tokens (99.1%) came from speculative cycles. The remaining 29 tokens are the boundary tokens of each request: 19 requests emitted exactly one token outside a cycle and 5 emitted two.

Each request carries exactly one no_provider fallback event, which is the first output token - the step before a speculative cycle has a provider. No request abandoned speculation mid-stream: first_fallback_position is unset for all 24 and the harness's rate-cliff detector found no request.

All 24 requests streamed a thinking block before any answer text, and 20 of 24 had emitted no answer text at all when the 128-token budget ran out (median thinking block 522 characters, median answer 0). The 128-token budget therefore measures decode throughput, not answer completeness.

Selected depth was 3 for nearly every cycle; 14 requests spent one cycle at depth 2 or 1 and 10 spent none. No request was limited by the 1,023-token MTP window: the longest prompt is 841 tokens and its request generated 127 tokens.

post_fix_pass.measurement_caveat: The c=8 harness arm's per-window decode rates are consumer-limited: its timeline shows 16-token windows at 2,100-2,500 tok/s for two requests, which is chunk-delivery burst after stream backpressure, not decode. The harness's aggregate rate (24.97 tok/s) and the vllm bench rate (27.23 tok/s) agree within 10%, so the aggregate is the trustworthy figure and the rate-cliff detector should not be read from that arm.

post_fix_pass.routing_change: At c=1 nothing changed: 24 of 24 requests still run MTP and 99.1% of output tokens still come from speculative cycles. At c=4 the pass became measurable at all (4 of 24 completing before, 24 of 24 after) and 5 requests ran MTP; at c=8, 11 of 24 ran MTP with 15.6% of output tokens from cycles. The remaining non-MTP reasons are no_provider and prompt_activation_in_flight, both recorded per request.
post_fix_pass.serving_metric_change: c=4 output throughput went from 8.70 tok/s with 16 of 24 requests failing to 28.39 tok/s with none failing; c=8 from 8.71 with 21 of 32 failing to 27.23 with none failing. c=1 is unchanged within run-to-run variance (20.68 before, 20.69 after).

ignore_eos=true.why: cycle termination and stop semantics are not wired for a request that must not stop on EOS

logit_bias, penalties other than identit.why: processors change the selected token, so the verifier would have to apply them at each verified position

logprobs / top_logprobs.why: token selection is unchanged under greedy, but the verified positions must expose the top-k logits the response contract promises

min_tokens.observed: rejected with 'min_tokens requires eos_token_id' (a coherent validation chain, not a silent downgrade)
min_tokens.why: min_tokens and eos_token_id are both on the incompatible list, so no route can be admitted

multi-token stop sequences.why: a cycle can cross a stop sequence inside the cycle, so the commit path would have to trim to the boundary

temperature > 0.impact: this is the setting real clients send most often, so it is the largest lost-opportunity item
temperature > 0.observed: route=default, decision_reason=sampling_mode_not_qualified, requested_route=speculative_mtp; 7.9 s for the probe against 2.9 s with MTP
temperature > 0.why: the verifier accepts a draft when it matches the target's greedy token, which is not the sampling distribution at temperature > 0; correct speculation needs a rejection test, which is not implemented

settings_classification.documentation_inconsistency: stop_token_ids is listed in SPECULATIVE_MTP_INCOMPATIBLE_CONDITIONS but the API rejects the parameter outright with HTTP 400 unsupported_parameter, so the condition can never be reached through the OpenAI surface.
settings_classification.method: One request per setting against a live default-configuration server (gfx1151, Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M, greedy unless stated), same prompt and 64-token budget, reading hipengine.generation_shape.route / .route_decision and hipengine.speculative_mtp.effective_route/.used.
settings_classification.not_a_blocker: The response contract already distinguishes selected from realized routing: a refused or downgraded request reports effective_route=default with used=false and a specific fallback_reason, alongside selected_route=speculative_mtp. The recorder did not capture effective_route, which is why the first pass read as a route that lied.

ttft_note: Three different first-token figures exist for this load and they measure different things. vLLM bench reports time to the first SSE chunk (3.04 ms at c=1), and the server opens the stream with a role-only chunk, so that is a first-byte figure. The recorder reports time to the first generated token of either channel: 1,150 ms median, 441 ms minimum, 4,314 ms on the first request of a cold server. Its earlier revision counted only delta.content, which for a thinking reply is the first answer token after the whole reasoning block, and that is the 5,961 ms median over the 4 requests of 24 that reached answer text within 128 tokens.
